title: Agentic RAG Knowledge Graph
kicker: Applied AI Research · Intel side project
summary: Hybrid search and structured reasoning over unstructured wikis, fusing Neo4j graphs with Chroma DB embeddings.
overview: An Agentic RAG pipeline that combines a Neo4j knowledge graph with Chroma DB vector embeddings, so an agent can both search semantically and walk explicit relationships across large, messy wiki repositories.
role: Designed and built the pipeline end to end: ingestion schemas, graph indexing recipes, retrieval, and context assembly.
outcomes: Hybrid retrieval that blends graph traversal with dense vector search.
Custom ingestion schemas and graph indexing recipes that preserve contextual relationships for evidence-backed answers.
Optimized retrieval latency and scaled context assembly for multi-turn AI reasoning.

title: REFL3CT Smart Platform
summary: A microservices platform with real-time state sync over WebSockets, built with FastAPI, React, SQLite, and Docker.
overview: REFL3CT is a full stack microservices platform that keeps distributed endpoints in sync in real time. Services talk over WebSockets and REST, run in Docker, and recover gracefully when connectivity drops.
role: Architected the platform and built persistent state management, session authentication, and failover logic, using agentic coding harnesses to speed up design and bug remediation.
outcomes: Real-time state synchronization via WebSockets and REST APIs.
Persistent state management, session auth, and failover connectivity across distributed endpoints.
LLM-assisted workflows for rapid prototyping, static analysis, and automated bug fixes.

title: AE2MES Automation Framework
summary: An event-driven automation harness in Lua with state-machine scheduling, resource management, and execution graphs.
overview: AE2MES is a modular, event-driven automation harness. A state-machine scheduler drives execution graphs while a resource manager keeps work flowing without contention.
role: Designed and implemented the harness, and used autonomous developer agents (Hermes Framework, Cursor CLI) to validate design patterns and run automated tests.
outcomes: State-machine scheduling and resource management in a modular, event-driven core.
Agent-driven automated testing and architectural verification.

title: Smart Mirror
summary: A Raspberry Pi smart mirror with a virtual try-on flow, a runtime image cache, a 10-job generation queue, notifications, and GPIO buttons.
overview: A team-built smart mirror running on a Raspberry Pi. You pick clothing items, snap a photo, and the mirror generates a virtual try-on. Images come from Cloudinary and are generated with Leonardo, so the work is cached and queued to keep the mirror responsive.
role: Led the virtual try-on user flow: the runtime cache, the async queue, the notification service, the 'Are you sure?' retake step, the try-on buttons for hats and shoes, and the GPIO button wiring.
outcomes: Runtime cache that downloads selected clothing images on demand and clears on shutdown, cutting Cloudinary and generation wait times.
Async queue of up to 10 pending try-on jobs, so users can batch-upload photos.
Screen-aware notifications when a try-on finishes or fails, plus a retake-or-reuse confirmation before generation.
Physical controls on GPIO pins 27, 22, and 17.

title: Smart Mirror Companion App
summary: The companion app for the Smart Mirror, with item management (CRUD) and a single-user mode.
overview: The Smart Mirror's companion app, where users manage the items the mirror works with.
role: Built the app's CRUD features and the single-user companion flow.
outcomes: Create, read, update, and delete flows for the mirror's data.
A single-user mode for the companion experience.

title: PiAQ Air-Quality Dashboard
summary: The frontend for a Raspberry Pi air-quality monitor, runnable locally on mock data.
overview: PiAQ is a team project that monitors air quality with a Raspberry Pi. I built the web frontend, which runs locally on mock data while the server and Pi routes come together.
role: Built the initial frontend UI and its communication layer, and laid out the roadmap for server routes, Pi data, AI interpretation, database linkage, and Twilio alerts.
outcomes: Working dashboard UI that runs with `npm install` and `npm run dev` on mock data.
Defined the next steps: server routes, sampling rate, AI interpretation, and phone alerts via Twilio.
